name: Vilsalpsee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Vilsalpsee at 1,165 m in the Tannheimer Tal is an emerald alpine jewel cradled in a pristine nature reserve beneath Gaishorn peak, with waterside trails and rustic pastures.
preis: Lakeshore trails freely accessible; vehicle access restricted by day (tourist road train and shuttles apply fares)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; prime hiking season runs May through October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The breathtaking Lake Vilsalpsee rests at an elevation of 1,165 metres at the cul-de-sac of a pristine tributary valley in the Tannheimer Tal, sheltered beneath the craggy limestone walls of the Allgäu Alps. Spanning 57 hectares with depths plunging to 47 metres, this protected body of water is celebrated as one of Western Austria's most awe-inspiring mountain sanctuaries. Towering peaks including Mount Gaishorn (2,247 m), Rauhhorn, and Rote Spitze mirror majestically in its sheltered, emerald-toned basin. Designated as a Natura 2000 European bird conservation area, the lake, peat moss wetlands, and dwarf-pine slopes shelter nesting great crested grebes and rare alpine amphibians. At the lake's headwall, the dramatic Berggaishorn waterfall plunges over towering rock slabs. Traditional dairy pastures including the Vilsalpe and the waterside Berggasthof Vilsalpsee combine raw nature with genuine Tyrolean alpine hospitality.

Route & Anforderungen

Circling Lake Vilsalpsee is an effortless scenic delight. The four-kilometre circuit takes approximately 1 to 1.5 hours of relaxed walking with almost no elevation change. The eastern shoreline path is paved and wide, whereas the western bank traces a root-ribbed forest track right against the water. Walkers departing directly from Tannheim village follow a gentle nature path along the Vils stream (approx. one hour walk each way). Standard sneakers suffice for the lake perimeter. However, ascending to the high cirque tarns of Lake Traualpsee (1,631 m) or conquering the Gaishorn peak strictly demands supportive, lug-soled mountain boots. The paved eastern shoreline is stroller-friendly.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists travel via federal highway B199 through the Tannheimer Tal to Tannheim village. Access by private motor vehicle along the Vilsalpsee access lane is strictly prohibited daily between 10:00 and 17:00. Visitors leave their cars at Tannheim's central car park and take the charming Alpen-Express road train, public buses, or horse-drawn carriages to the lake.

Tipps

Hike to the far end of the lake basin to marvel at the Berggaishorn waterfall, which plunges over 100 vertical metres down sheer rock amphitheaters. Afterwards, visit the historic Vilsalpe pasture to taste freshly churned buttermilk and artisan alpine cheese.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (während der Wintermonate Zufahrt teilweise eingeschränkt)
